prompt: I have 100% increased fire damage from the tree and a support gem that says 30% more fire damage. A friend says I should just add them up to 130%. Is he right, and how do the two combine?

must: Says the friend is wrong: the two do not add to 130%
Says increased modifiers are summed into one multiplier and each more modifier multiplies separately
Gives the result: base x (1 + 1.00) x 1.30 = 2.6 times base damage (260% of base, a 160% net gain)
must_not: Adds increased and more together
Gives 130% or 2.3 times as the result

intent: Tests whether 'increased' and 'more' modifiers are combined correctly.

prompt: My skill has 40% of Physical converted to Cold, and I also have an item that converts 60% of Physical to Fire and a jewel converting 50% of Physical to Lightning. How much of my physical damage ends up as each type?

must: Gives the split: 40% cold, about 32.7% fire, about 27.3% lightning, 0% left as physical
Says total conversion from one type cannot exceed 100%
Says the skill's own conversion (40% to cold) is applied first and is not scaled down
Says the other sources (60% fire and 50% lightning, 110% in total) are scaled in proportion to fit the remaining 60%
must_not: Scales the skill's conversion down along with the item and jewel
Lets conversion exceed 100% or leaves physical damage over
Says the converted cold or lightning converts further without a modifier that does so

intent: Tests conversion order and handling of conversion totals above 100%.

prompt: I convert all my physical damage to cold. Do my 'increased physical damage' modifiers still help my cold damage?

must: Says yes: increased physical damage still scales the converted cold damage
Says converted damage keeps its original type for scaling, so modifiers to physical and to cold both apply
Says the physical and cold increases add together in one increased total (for example 50% and 50% make 100% increased)
Separates global increased physical damage (applies to the converted damage) from a weapon's local increased physical damage (only raises that weapon's base before conversion)
must_not: Says physical modifiers stop applying after conversion
Multiplies the physical and cold increases as separate multipliers

intent: Tests which modifiers apply to damage after conversion.

prompt: What's the difference between 'gain 20% of physical damage as extra fire damage' and converting 20% of physical to fire? Which is better on a physical attack build?

must: Says gained as extra adds fire damage on top and leaves the physical damage whole (100 physical with 20% as extra fire is 100 physical plus 20 fire)
Says conversion moves part of the physical damage to fire, so the total before scaling is unchanged (100 physical with 20% converted is 80 physical plus 20 fire)
Says gained as extra is usually the better raw damage gain on a physical attack build
Says conversion adds no damage by itself; it changes which modifiers scale the damage and how the enemy mitigates it, and is chosen to use elemental scaling, penetration or elemental ailments
must_not: Treats the two as the same thing
Says conversion alone raises total damage

intent: Tests gained-as-extra versus conversion and how each interacts with scaling.

prompt: Can fire damage that was converted from cold be converted back into cold, or gain extra cold damage from itself?

must: Says no: fire converted from cold cannot be converted back into cold, and cannot gain extra cold damage from itself
Gives the one-way order physical, lightning, cold, fire, chaos; steps can be skipped but never reversed
Says there are no loops: once damage has moved to a later type it stays there
Says the converted fire damage still scales with both cold and fire modifiers
must_not: Says damage can convert backwards or loop
Says converted damage loses the scaling of its original type

intent: Tests the direction of the conversion chain and whether damage can loop.

prompt: I have 20,000 armour. Why do I still take nearly full damage from a big boss slam but almost nothing from trash mobs?

must: Says armour's reduction depends on the size of the physical hit: the bigger the hit, the smaller the share armour removes
Gives the formula: reduction = armour / (armour + 5 x damage), or states the same relation in words
Says small hits from trash monsters are reduced by a very large share, near the cap, while a boss slam of thousands of damage is reduced far less by the same armour
Says armour does nothing against elemental or chaos damage or physical damage over time, which many boss hits include
Recommends layers beyond armour, such as endurance charges, physical damage taken as elemental, life, block, suppression or evasion
must_not: Says armour gives a fixed percentage reduction whatever the hit size
Says armour reduces elemental or chaos damage

intent: Tests the armour formula's dependence on hit size.

prompt: How much physical damage reduction can I get from armour and endurance charges at most, and what happens to anything past that cap?

must: Says physical damage reduction from armour plus additional physical damage reduction (such as endurance charges) is capped at 90%
Says endurance charges add 4% physical damage reduction each, summed with armour's reduction before the cap (each also gives 4% elemental damage reduction)
Says reduction above 90% does nothing by itself: 110% behaves like 90%
Says the one use of excess reduction is as a buffer against enemy Overwhelm or similar penalties, which are subtracted before the cap is applied
Says going past the cap needs separate layers that apply at a later step, such as less or reduced damage taken modifiers (fortification for example) or physical damage taken as another damage type
must_not: Says the cap is 75% or any figure other than 90%
Says endurance charges multiply with armour or are capped separately from it
Says endurance charges still give elemental resistances (changed in 3.25.0)

intent: Tests the physical damage reduction cap and how sources combine.

prompt: Why does my ignite sometimes do tiny damage, or my chill barely slow, on pinnacle bosses even though my hits are big? How does a boss's ailment threshold change things?

must: Says chill (and the other non-damaging ailments) scales with the hit's damage of the matching type compared with the target's ailment threshold, not with how big the hit looks
Says the threshold is tied to maximum life: equal to life for normal monsters, and adjusted for bosses but still very high, so the same cold hit is a tiny fraction of a pinnacle boss's threshold
Says chill has a minimum effect of 5% below which it is not applied, and a default maximum of 30%

Says ignite is calculated separately from the hit: it comes from the hit's base fire damage and is scaled by fire, damage over time, burning and ignite modifiers, not by the critical strike multiplier or modifiers that only affect hits
Says a big hit built on crit multiplier, hit-only modifiers or non-fire damage therefore gives a weak ignite
Gives the fix: for chill or freeze, more cold damage per hit or increased effect of non-damaging ailments; for ignite, more base fire damage and ignite or damage over time scaling
must_not: Says ignite damage depends on the boss's ailment threshold
Says the critical strike multiplier scales ignite
Says a boss's ailment threshold always equals its full life
Uses the hit's total damage, not its cold part, for chill

intent: Tests ailment threshold and how it affects ailments on high-life enemies.

prompt: How does the chance to shock or freeze an enemy relate to how much of its life the hit deals? Does a freeze last longer when I hit harder?

must: Separates chance from size: chance to freeze or shock only decides whether the ailment is attempted on a non-critical hit, and critical strikes always attempt both

Says that even at 100% chance the result depends on the hit's cold damage (freeze) or lightning damage (shock) compared with the target's ailment threshold, which is its maximum life for most monsters
Says yes, a harder cold hit freezes longer: 0.06 seconds per 1% of the threshold dealt as cold
Says a freeze needs at least 0.3 seconds, which is 5% of the threshold in one hit, or it does not happen, and that the base maximum is 3 seconds, reached at 50% of the threshold
Says shock's effect scales with the lightning damage relative to the threshold, from a 5% minimum below which no shock is applied up to a default maximum of 50% increased damage taken
must_not: Says a higher chance to freeze or shock makes the freeze longer or the shock stronger
Says 100% chance guarantees a freeze or shock whatever the hit's size
Uses the hit's total damage, not its cold or lightning part

intent: Tests how hit size drives shock effect and freeze duration.

prompt: I have 5% of physical attack damage leeched as life. Does stacking more leech percentage make me recover faster?

must: Says more leech percentage only helps up to a ceiling: past the cap it does not raise recovery per second
Says each hit makes its own leech instance, which recovers at a base 2% of maximum life per second and can recover at most 10% of maximum life in total by default
Says all life leech instances together are capped at 20% of maximum life per second by default
Says below the cap more leech percentage does help, because each instance holds more and instances overlap for longer; at the cap (fast hits, many targets or high damage) the extra is ignored
Names what does raise recovery past the cap: a higher maximum total life recovery per second from leech, increased total recovery per second from leech, or instant leech
must_not: Says recovery per second keeps rising in proportion to leech percentage with no cap
Says a bigger hit makes a single leech instance recover faster
Gives default caps other than 20% per second total and 10% per instance for life

intent: Tests leech instances, leech rate, and the leech rate cap.

prompt: When exactly does my energy shield start recharging after taking damage, and what resets the delay? Does a damage-over-time effect stop it?

must: Says energy shield recharge starts 2 seconds after you last took damage, by default
Says faster start of energy shield recharge shortens the delay: delay = 2 s / (1 + faster start), the same as 200 / (100 + r) for r% faster start
Says taking any new damage, to energy shield or to life, resets the delay from that moment and stops a recharge that is running
Says yes, damage over time counts: ignite, poison or bleed keeps interrupting recharge until it stops dealing damage
Says energy shield regeneration (and leech) is a separate source that damage over time does not interrupt
must_not: Says damage over time does not interrupt recharge
Says only damage to energy shield itself resets the delay
Treats energy shield recharge and energy shield regeneration as the same thing

intent: Tests energy shield recharge delay, interruption rules, and recharge rate.

prompt: My crit chance on the tooltip is 45% but it feels like I crit less than that against bosses. How do accuracy and crit interact?

must: Says an attack that rolls a critical strike must pass a second accuracy check, and if it fails the hit lands as a normal, non-critical hit
Gives the result: effective crit chance = crit chance x chance to hit that enemy (45% x 80% = 36% in the example, or the same idea with other numbers)
Says bosses have more evasion than the monsters the character sheet assumes, so both hit chance and effective crit chance are lower against them
Says this applies to attacks only: spells do not use accuracy
Gives the fix: raise chance to hit toward 100% with accuracy rating (Precision is one source), lower the enemy's evasion (blind for example), or use hits that cannot be evaded
Suggests checking the real hit chance and effective crit chance against a boss in Path of Building or the app's calculation, not the in-game sheet
must_not: Says accuracy has no effect on critical strikes
Says a crit that fails the second check becomes a miss
Says spells lose crit chance to evasion

intent: Tests how hit chance and critical strike chance combine into effective crits.

prompt: If I have +100% to critical strike multiplier on my gear, what is my total multiplier, and how does it scale compared with 'increased critical strike chance'?

must: Says the base critical strike multiplier is 150%, and +% to critical strike multiplier is additive with it and with other sources, so +100% gives 250% (a crit deals 2.5 times a normal hit)

Says increased critical strike chance multiplies the base crit chance of the weapon or skill; it is not added to the percentage: (base + added) x (1 + increased) x more, so 5% base with 100% increased is 10%
Says crit chance is capped at 100%
Says the two depend on each other: multiplier only matters on hits that crit, so its value grows with crit chance, and crit chance is worth more the higher the multiplier
Advises getting crit chance to a dependable level before or alongside stacking multiplier
must_not: Says the total is 200%, or 100%, by forgetting or misusing the 150% base
Says +100% multiplier doubles the multiplier (150% x 2 = 300%)
Says 100% increased critical strike chance adds 100 percentage points of crit chance

intent: Tests base critical strike multiplier and the difference between chance and multiplier scaling.

prompt: Should I go for spell block or spell suppression as a melee character? What does each actually do to a spell that hits me?

must: Says spell suppression is a chance per spell hit (not attacks, not damage over time), capped at 100%; a suppressed spell still hits but a share of its damage is prevented, 40% by default since 3.27.0, and the ailments from that hit are reduced by the same share
Says at 100% chance every spell hit is reduced, which makes suppression predictable

Says spell block is a chance to take no damage at all from a spell hit, and a blocked hit applies no on-hit effects such as ailments; a hit that is not blocked deals full damage, so block is all-or-nothing and can fail in streaks
Says spell block is capped at 75% by default

Says the choice depends on the build: suppression suits evasion or dexterity builds on the right side of the tree, spell block suits strength, armour or shield builds where suppression is far away, backed by other mitigation and recovery on block
Says the two are separate layers that can be used together
must_not: Says suppression prevents 50% of spell damage by default (the value before 3.27.0)
Says suppression makes a spell miss or stops it completely
Says suppression works against attacks or damage over time
Adds suppression chance and spell block chance together as one number

intent: Tests spell block versus spell suppression, their caps, and their effect on a hit.

prompt: I have +1 to maximum curses. I put Frostbite and Elemental Weakness on my gear and Vulnerability on hit. Only two of them seem to show on the enemy. Why, and how do I raise the number?

must: Says the default curse limit is one, so with +1 to maximum curses the limit is two
Says three different curses are being applied against a limit of two, so only two stay on the enemy: a new curse over the limit replaces an older one
Says all three at once needs a limit of three, which is one more +1 to maximum number of curses
Names where more curse limit comes from: the passive tree (Whispers of Doom is the usual example), item modifiers, or unique items, and tells the user to check current sources through the tools
must_not: Says the default curse limit is two or more
Says curse effect, curse duration or a higher gem level lets more curses stay on an enemy
Says the three curses cannot be on one enemy whatever the limit

intent: Tests the curse limit, how new curses replace old ones, and the sources that raise the limit.

prompt: My Raise Zombie build has 'minions deal 20% increased damage' on a jewel. If I also take '20% increased damage' on the tree, does that boost my zombies too?

must: Says no: a plain '20% increased damage' on the tree applies to the character's own damage and does not reach the zombies
Says a modifier affects minions only if its text says so: 'minions deal', 'minions have', a line naming you and your minions or allies, or an aura or other ally buff
Says the 'minions deal 20% increased damage' jewel does apply to the zombies
Says the link that exists runs the other way: Spiritual Aid makes increases and reductions to minion damage also affect you, and it does not make your own damage modifiers affect minions
must_not: Says generic increased damage on the tree boosts minions
Says the two 20% lines add together for the zombies
Says Spiritual Aid makes the character's damage modifiers apply to minions

intent: Tests which player modifiers apply to minions.

prompt: I'm using Cast on Critical Strike with Arc. Why doesn't Arc trigger on every crit? What limits the trigger rate, and does cast speed help?
intent: Tests trigger cooldowns and what scales a triggered spell's rate.

prompt: Does 'damage over time multiplier' affect my ignite, and how is it different from 'increased burning damage'?
intent: Tests damage over time multiplier versus increased damage.

prompt: How does chance to evade work in PoE1? If my evasion chance is 60%, can I get hit several times in a row?
intent: Tests how evasion is rolled in PoE1 and which hits it applies to.

prompt: I'm at 75% fire resistance. The map has -12% maximum resistances. What is my actual fire resistance and how much more damage do I take?
intent: Tests maximum versus current resistance and the effect of losing resistance on damage taken.
